definitions.explanation: The state of the tide when the water reaches its lowest level. Occurs approximately twice daily, exposing areas of the seafloor that are normally underwater.

examples.japanese: {干潮|かんちょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時|とき}→時：02918_toki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{潮干狩|しおひが}り→潮干狩り：18507_shiohigari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}こう→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Let's go clam digging at low tide.

examples.japanese: {干潮|かんちょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{海底|かいてい}→海底：13287_kaitei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えて→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The seafloor is visible at low tide.

examples.japanese: {干潮|かんちょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{待|ま}とう→待つ：00469_matsu⟧。

examples.english: There's a sandy path that you can only cross at low tide.

examples.japanese: {干潮|かんちょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{干潟|ひがた}→干潟：05592_higata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{現|あらわ}れて→現れる：01870_arawareru⟧、⟦カニ→蟹：04325_kani⟧⟦や→や：10080_ya⟧⟦{貝|かい}→貝：02145_kai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{観察|かんさつ}→観察：02558_kansatsu⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: When the tide goes out, tidal flats appear and you can observe crabs and shellfish.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
・{干|かん} (dry) + {潮|ちょう} (tide)

RELATED TERMS:
・{満潮|まんちょう} (high tide) - antonym
・{引|ひ}き{潮|しお} (ebb tide/receding tide)
・{潮|しお}が{引|ひ}く (tide goes out)
・{干潟|ひがた} (tidal flat - exposed at low tide)

ACTIVITIES AT LOW TIDE:
・{潮干狩|しおひが}り (clam digging) - popular spring activity
・{磯|いそ}{遊|あそ}び (tidepooling)
・{海|うみ}の{生|い}き{物|もの}{観察|かんさつ} (observing sea creatures)

SAFETY NOTE:
・Be aware of rising tides when exploring tidal areas
・Check tide tables ({潮見表|しおみひょう}) before coastal activities
・Some areas become dangerous paths at high tide

FISHING CONTEXT:
・Certain fish are more active during specific tidal phases
・{潮|しお}{回|まわ}り (tidal cycle) important for fishing

COLLOCATIONS:
・{干潮|かんちょう}になる (to become low tide)
・{干潮|かんちょう}の{時刻|じこく} (time of low tide)
・{干潮|かんちょう}{時|じ} (at low tide)
